subject: Zero-touch access runbook + cutover cadence for Clearsky (SSO/SCIM/IP/service-accounts)
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Clearsky Security <security@clearsky.ai>, Priya Menon <priya@clearsky.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Dec 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Zero-touch access runbook + cutover cadence for Clearsky (SSO/SCIM/IP/service-accounts)

Hi Priya / Rahul —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our onboarding checklist, we want to align on a low-friction cutover for Clearsky’s enterprise environment that preserves sessions and reduces ops lift on your side (zero-touch where possible). I’ve attached a short runbook draft and a proposed cadence — please review and flag any hard constraints. Key items we want confirmed before engineering kickoff: 

- SSO / SAML
  - Production IdP metadata endpoint (entityID / metadata URL) and any required cert rotation cadence.
  - Are there any custom attributes you rely on that we should map (eduPersonPrincipalName / custom:employee_id)?

- SCIM
  - Scope: would you like full SCIM provisioning (create/update/deactivate) or just group sync?
  - SCIM schema notes attached (scim-schema-v2.csv); please call out any non-standard mappings.

- IP allowlist
  - Please confirm your firewall: public IPs/CIDRs we'll be whitelisting for API calls (we prefer a short, static range for Dedicated traffic).

- Service accounts & org policies
  - Number of service accounts you want us to provision vs. reuse existing tokens. Naming convention?
  - Any org-level constraints (SAML-enforced MFA, session duration limits) we need to respect on cutover.

Proposed timeline (all times PST):
- Day 0: Confirm metadata + SCIM scope + IP list
- Day 1: Engineering ingestion of SAML metadata + test IdP flow against staging
- Day 3: SCIM test provisioning with sample users (non-prod)
- Day 5: Production cutover window (2-hour maintenance window) with rollback plan

Attachments: access-runbook-draft.pdf (PDF) — includes rollback steps; scim-schema-v2.csv — suggested attribute map.

Ask: Can you send the metadata URL and current allowlist before EOD Friday? If you prefer a quick 20-min sync, I can schedule with Jonas and Neha.

Thanks,
Mina
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Zero-touch access runbook + cutover cadence for Clearsky (SSO/SCIM/IP/service-accounts)

Hi Mina —

Thanks for the clear plan — this looks good. Quick answers below: 

- SAML metadata: https://idp.clearsky.ai/metadata.xml (will send cert thumbprint separately). Our IdP rotates certs quarterly — we can provide a notification webhook if that helps.
- Mapping: we use employeeNumber (custom) and department in assertions; not using eduPerson.
- SCIM scope: prefer full provisioning for users (create/update/deactivate), but we only want group sync for admin groups. We’ve attached our current IP list for API consumption (clearsky-current-ips.txt).
- Service accounts: two dedicated service accounts (one for provisioning, one for auditing). Naming: clearsky-scim-provisioner, clearsky-audit-sa.
- Org policies: session lifetime enforced at 8 hours; MFA required for admins only.

Questions from our infra team: how does Redwood handle partial SCIM failures (e.g., email collisions)? Also, do you support SCIM delta syncs or only full-sync endpoints?

We’re OK with your Day 5 window — prefer mornings PST. I’ll loop in Rahul (infra) for any port/ACL work.

—Priya
Dir. Platform Engineering, Clearsky AI

Mina / Neha —

Thanks for the context and Clearsky’s answers. Quick engineering plan and acceptance criteria: 

1) SAML ingestion
   - We will fetch the metadata URL and validate cert chain. We’ll add a watch job to surface cert expiry (since they rotate quarterly). Acceptance: successful full SSO login in staging with their assertion including employeeNumber and department.

2) SCIM provisioning
   - We support incremental (delta) SCIM with change tokens. For collisions (email already exists) we’ll attempt attribute merge; if merge fails we create a remediation ticket and put the user in a dead-letter queue. Acceptance: staged provisioning of 50 test users with 0 critical errors and documented remediation flow.

3) IP allowlist
   - We’ll consume the clearsky-current-ips.txt and add those CIDRs to our customer firewall rule. We’ll also expose a small egress check endpoint in staging for their infra to verify connectivity. Acceptance: Clearsky can call staging API from their CIDRs successfully.

4) Service accounts & org policies
   - Provision two scoped service accounts as named. We’ll apply least-privilege roles and rotate keys per our default (90d), but we can accept their rotation webhook to trigger pre-rotation notifications. Acceptance: both service accounts can perform intended actions in staging and have audit logging enabled.

Cutover checklist (high-level) — I’ll drop a final doc into the shared Drive folder and we’ll attach the runbook, but short checklist:
   - Ingest metadata + validate cert
   - Smoke SSO login (admin/non-admin)
   - Run SCIM provisioning test (50 users)
   - Verify IP allowlist connectivity
   - Provision service accounts and confirm audit logs
   - Production cutover during 2-hr window; monitor 15-min token metrics and error rates for 2 hours post-cutover

I’ll prepare the cutover checklist and the small script we use for SCIM retry logic (will attach in the Drive). If Monday sync works, I can join and run through the staging verification with Clearsky infra.

-Jonas
Engineering Manager | Redwood Inference
